'''Utari Shrine''' (うたりじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Kosakai-chō, Aza Miyawaki, {{ill|Toyokawa, Aichi|Q389495|qid=Q389495}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}}, it was designated as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine enshrines the following single deity:
* Unakami Sukune no Mikoto (うなかみすくねのみこと)

=== History ===
The enshrined deity, Unakami Sukune no Mikoto, is said to be a descendant of {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|Q333572|qid=Q333572}}, the great-great-grandchild (fourth generation) of {{ill|Katsuragi Sotsuhiko|Q11620922|qid=Q11620922}}. During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}}, he was appointed as {{ill|provincial governor of Hono no Kuni (present-day Higashi-Mikawa)|Q11597049|qid=Q11597049|lt=provincial governor of Hono no Kuni (present-day Higashi-Mikawa)}}. Katsuragi Sotsuhiko no Mikoto was the father of {{ill|Princess Iwa|Q1066593|qid=Q1066593}}, the empress of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ar|الإمبراطور نينتوكو|arz|الامبراطور نينتوكو|azb|نینتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট নিন্তকু|br|Impalaer Nintoku|ca|Emperador Nintoku|cs|Nintoku|de|Nintoku|es|Nintoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور نینتوکو|fi|Nintoku|fr|Nintoku|hr|Nintoku|hu|Nintoku japán császár|id|Kaisar Nintoku|it|Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|ka|ნინტოკუ|ko|닌토쿠 천황|lt|Imperatorius Nintoku|ms|Maharaja Nintoku|nds|Nintoku|nl|Nintoku|pl|Nintoku|pt|Nintoku|ru|Император Нинтоку|sh|Car Nintoku|simple|Emperor Nintoku|sl|Cesar Nintoku|sv|Nintoku|th|จักรพรรดินินโตกุ|tl|Emperador Nintoku|tr|Nintoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Нінтоку|uz|Imperator Nintoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Nintoku|yo|Emperor Nintoku|zh|仁德天皇|zh_min_nan|Nintoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|仁德天皇|qid=Q313119}}, and is said to have wielded great power as a {{ill|Gōzoku|Q84066|qid=Q84066}} of Katsuragi in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}. After his death, Unakami Sukune no Mikoto was enshrined at Kashiwagi Beach in Hirai, {{ill|Mikawa Province|Q768158|qid=Q768158}}, in recognition of his outstanding achievements in promoting industry and governing the people. It is said that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}, in the 15th year of the {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} ({{ill|686|Q30619|qid=Q30619}}), on {{ill|April 11|Q2501|qid=Q2501}}, the shrine was relocated to its present site by Hata no Ishikatsu (はたのいしかつ).

In the 6th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635}} ({{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}}), the shrine’s {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|fa|شینکای (رتبه الهی)|ja|神階|qid=Q11591025}} was promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and its name appears in the Jinmyōchō of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}. During the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, when the Emperor made his eastern progress, the shrine received an imperial envoy. In the 11th year of the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1878|Q7776|qid=Q7776}}), it received a shrine name scroll in the imperial handwriting of {{ill|Prince Arisugawa Taruhito|Q668338|qid=Q668338}}. In the 7th year of the {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} ({{ill|1918|Q2094|qid=Q2094}}), it was elevated from a village shrine to a prefectural shrine.

=== Festivals ===
* Wind Festival (Kazematsuri) – Held every year on the second Saturday and Sunday of April. {{ill|Tezutsu-hanabi|Q11497105|qid=Q11497105}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=launched fireworks}}, and {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} are dedicated. This festival is the origin of the name {{ill|Kozakai Kifukan|Q108765371|qid=Q108765371}}.
* Rice Paddy Festival – Held on the 7th day of the 1st month of the lunar calendar.
